claim: mRNA profiles were measured in 15 yeast species from the phylum Ascomycota to reconstruct the evolution of their modular regulatory programs along a time course of growth on glucose over 300 million years.
source_text: Here, we used a phylogenetic framework to measure mRNA profiles in 15 yeast species from the phylum Ascomycota and reconstruct the evolution of their modular regulatory programs along a time course of growth on glucose over 300 million years.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental measurements of mRNA profiles across 15 species as described in the manuscript.

claim: Modules have diverged proportionally to phylogenetic distance.
source_text: We found that modules have diverged proportionally to phylogenetic distance
evidence_reasoning: This finding is based on analysis of the experimental data showing correlation between module divergence and phylogenetic distance.

claim: Prominent changes in gene regulation accompany changes in lifestyle and ploidy, especially in carbon metabolism.
source_text: with prominent changes in gene regulation accompanying changes in lifestyle and ploidy, especially in carbon metabolism.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the experimental data showing coordinated changes in gene expression patterns associated with lifestyle and ploidy changes.

claim: Paralogs have significantly contributed to regulatory divergence, typically within a very short window from their duplication.
source_text: Paralogs have significantly contributed to regulatory divergence, typically within a very short window from their duplication.
evidence_reasoning: This is based on analysis of paralogous genes showing increased reassignment shortly after duplication events.

claim: Paralogs from a whole genome duplication (WGD) event have a uniquely substantial contribution that extends over a longer span.
source_text: Paralogs from a whole genome duplication (WGD) event have a uniquely substantial contribution that extends over a longer span.
evidence_reasoning: This finding is based on comparative analysis of WGD paralogs versus sporadic duplicates showing different temporal patterns of divergence.

claim: Similar patterns occur when considering the evolution of the heat shock regulatory program measured in eight of the species.
source_text: Similar patterns occur when considering the evolution of the heat shock regulatory program measured in eight of the species, suggesting that these are general evolutionary principles.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental measurements of heat shock response in eight species showing comparable evolutionary patterns.

claim: Divergence in gene regulation can play a major role in evolution.
source_text: Divergence in gene regulation can play a major role in evolution.
evidence_reasoning: This is a general principle supported by citations to previous work and established scientific knowledge.

claim: Examples of regulatory differences between species were described in bacteria, fungi, flies, and mammals.
source_text: Examples of regulatory differences between species were described in a wide range of species including bacteria (McAdams et al., 2004), fungi (Gasch et al., 2004; Habib et al., 2012), flies (Prud'homme et al., 2007; Wittkopp et al., 2008; Bradley et al., 2010), and mammals (Khaitovich et al., 2006; Odom et al., 2007; Brawand et al., 2011; Lindblad-Toh et al., 2011; Perry et al., 2012).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous studies in different organisms.

claim: The mechanisms through which regulatory systems evolve are still only partially understood.
source_text: However, the mechanisms through which regulatory systems evolve are still only partially understood
evidence_reasoning: This reflects the current state of scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: In most cases the adaptive importance of regulatory changes is unknown.
source_text: and in most cases the adaptive importance of regulatory changes is unknown
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations and reflects current limitations in understanding regulatory evolution.

claim: Gene duplication can promote regulatory divergence by either neo-functionalization or sub-functionalization of regulatory mechanisms of the two paralogs.
source_text: it has been suggested (Lynch and Force, 2000; Gu et al., 2004, 2005; Teichmann and Babu, 2004; ; Conant and Wolfe, 2006; Tirosh and Barkai, 2007; Wapinski et al., 2007b) that gene duplication can promote regulatory divergence by either neo-functionalization or sub-functionalization of regulatory mechanisms of the two paralogs.
evidence_reasoning: This is a theoretical model supported by multiple citations to previous work.

claim: The 15 Ascomycota species in the study span >300 million years of evolution.
source_text: Here, we use comparative transcriptional studies across 15 Ascomycota species—spanning >300 million years of evolution (Sipiczki, 2000)
evidence_reasoning: The time span is based on a cited phylogenetic study.

claim: Species in the Kluyveromyces, Candida, and Yarrowia clades are respiratory and use oxidative phosphorylation.
source_text: Species in the Kluyveromyces, Candida, and Yarrowia clades are respiratory and use oxidative phosphorylation (Figure 1A, red and green).
evidence_reasoning: This is based on established knowledge about these species and confirmed by the experimental observations.

claim: A respiro-fermentative lifestyle has evolved independently at least twice in this phylogeny, once after the WGD and once in Schizosaccharomyces.
source_text: Conversely, a respiro-fermentative lifestyle—a preference to ferment glucose even in the presence of oxygen (Piskur et al., 2006)—has evolved independently at least twice in this phylogeny, once after the WGD (Conant and Wolfe, 2007) and once in Schizosaccharomyces (Rhind et al., 2011)
evidence_reasoning: This evolutionary inference is supported by citations and phylogenetic analysis.

claim: K. polysporus has an intermediate phenotype between respiro-fermentative and respiratory.
source_text: K. polysporus, the most basal post-WGD species (Scannell et al., 2007) has an intermediate phenotype between respiro-fermentative and respiratory
evidence_reasoning: This is based on experimental observations and phylogenetic position from cited work.

claim: Y. lipolytica is an obligate respiratory species that can uniquely use normal hydrocarbons and various fats as carbon sources.
source_text: Y. lipolytica (Figure 1A, green) is an obligate respiratory species, but can uniquely use normal hydrocarbons and various fats as carbon sources (Kurtzman, 2000).
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about Y. lipolytica supported by citation.

claim: The optimized growth medium boosts the growth of otherwise slow growers without substantially impacting the growth of fast growers.
source_text: Our formulation boosts the growth of otherwise slow growers, without substantially impacting the growth of fast growers
evidence_reasoning: This is based on experimental measurements of growth in different media.

claim: Approximately 300 expression profiles were collected at six physiologically comparable time points along each species' growth.
source_text: and collected ∼300 expression profiles at six physiologically comparable time points along each species' growth: repletion (lag phase), exponential growth ('mid-log' and 'late log'), the point of glucose depletion ('diauxic shift') and two later time points when the growth rate levels off ('post shift' and 'plateau').
evidence_reasoning: This describes the experimental design and data collection.

claim: Arboretum is a new algorithm used to identify expression modules across species and to reconstruct their evolutionary history.
source_text: To analyze the evolution of regulatory modules, we use a new algorithm, Arboretum (Roy et al., 2013), to identify expression modules across species and to reconstruct their evolutionary history.
evidence_reasoning: This describes a computational method developed and cited.

claim: The degree of divergence of the transcriptional profiles correlates with phylogenetic distance.
source_text: We find that the degree of divergence of the transcriptional profiles correlates with phylogenetic distance
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from statistical analysis of the experimental data.

claim: The largest divergence in transcriptional profiles occurs in lag phase.
source_text: with the largest divergence in lag phase profiles.
evidence_reasoning: This is based on analysis of expression profiles across different growth phases.

claim: In all species, the transcriptional response involves five major transcriptional modules.
source_text: In all species, the transcriptional response involves five major transcriptional modules.
evidence_reasoning: This is based on Arboretum analysis of the expression data across all species.

claim: While the module's expression patterns are conserved across species, their gene membership diverges, proportionally to phylogenetic distance.
source_text: While the module's expression patterns are conserved across species, their gene membership diverges, proportionally to phylogenetic distance.
evidence_reasoning: This is based on Arboretum analysis showing conservation of patterns but divergence in membership.

claim: Gene duplication events significantly contribute to regulatory divergence, in particular close to their phylogenetic point of duplication.
source_text: Gene duplication events significantly contribute to regulatory divergence, in particular close to their phylogenetic point of duplication.
evidence_reasoning: This is based on analysis of paralogous genes and their module reassignment patterns.

claim: This contribution is more pronounced and more prolonged for WGD paralogs.
source_text: This contribution is more pronounced and more prolonged for WGD paralogs.
evidence_reasoning: This is based on comparative analysis of WGD versus sporadic duplicates.

claim: The correlation in expression decreases with phylogenetic distance at each of the time points.
source_text: We found that the degree of correlation is inversely related with the phylogenetic distance between the species (r<−0.39 to −0.77, p<3 × 10−5, Figure 3B–F), such that the closer two species are in the phylogeny, the higher the correlation between their profiles. This inverse relation is apparent at each of the time points
evidence_reasoning: This is a statistical finding from correlation analysis of expression profiles.

claim: Profiles at diauxic shift, post shift and plateau are the most correlated between species.
source_text: Profiles at diauxic shift, post shift and plateau are the most correlated between species (Figure 3D–G)
evidence_reasoning: This is based on correlation analysis of expression profiles at different time points.

claim: The lag profiles, when cells 'reset' in response to nutrient repletion, are the most divergent.
source_text: whereas the lag profiles, when cells 'reset' in response to nutrient repletion, are the most divergent (Figure 3B,G), likely reflecting species-specific responses to nutrient signals shaped by niche adaptation.
evidence_reasoning: This is based on correlation analysis with an inference about the biological reason.

claim: S. japonicus and S. castellii were the most divergent species.
source_text: S. japonicus and S. castellii were the most divergent, such that in some cases, their Lag phase profiles were even anti-correlated to those of other species, suggesting distinct repletion programs.
evidence_reasoning: This is based on correlation analysis showing anti-correlation in some cases.

claim: Arboretum uses a generative probabilistic model of the evolution of module membership of a given gene, starting from the last common ancestor (LCA) of a set of species.
source_text: Arboretum uses a generative probabilistic model of the evolution of module membership of a given gene, starting from the last common ancestor (LCA) of a set of species and probabilistically propagating this membership down the branches of the phylogenetic tree to the leaf nodes.
evidence_reasoning: This describes the computational method as cited.

claim: Arboretum uses the phylogeny to link the module IDs at each phylogenetic point to the modules of the LCA.
source_text: Arboretum uses the phylogeny to link the module IDs at each phylogenetic point to the modules of the LCA, and uses the structures of gene trees (as defined from genome sequences; Wapinski et al., 2007a) during module identification.
evidence_reasoning: This describes the computational method as cited.

claim: Arboretum allows genes to change their module assignment during evolution.
source_text: Arboretum allows genes to change their module assignment during evolution, but at any ancestral or extant species, every gene (if present in that species) must be assigned to exactly one module for a particular response.
evidence_reasoning: This describes a feature of the computational method.

claim: Module 1 consists of genes involved in ribosome biogenesis and is strongly repressed following glucose depletion.
source_text: Module 1 (bright blue) consists of genes involved in ribosome biogenesis and is strongly repressed following glucose depletion
evidence_reasoning: This is based on Arboretum analysis and GO enrichment of the module.

claim: Module 5 consists of genes involved in respiration and stress response and is strongly induced following glucose depletion.
source_text: Module 5 (red) consists of genes involved in respiration and stress response and is strongly induced following glucose depletion
evidence_reasoning: This is based on Arboretum analysis and GO enrichment of the module.

claim: Modules 2, 3, and 4 have intermediate expression patterns.
source_text: Modules 2, 3, and 4 have intermediate expression patterns
evidence_reasoning: This is based on Arboretum analysis of expression patterns.

claim: Modules conserve their gene members relative to those of their immediately ancestral internal vertex in the tree, inversely to phylogenetic distance.
source_text: Modules conserve their gene members relative to those of their immediately ancestral internal vertex in the tree ('immediate ancestor'), inversely to phylogenetic distance.
evidence_reasoning: This is based on analysis of module conservation using the AMCI metric.

claim: The AMCI is calculated as the mean of the diagonal entries of the transition matrix.
source_text: The AMCI is calculated as the mean of the diagonal entries.
evidence_reasoning: This is a definition of the computational metric used.

claim: The AMCI decreases with increased phylogenetic distance.
source_text: The correlation between branch length and AMCI is −0.68 (p≤1.13 −× 10−4).
evidence_reasoning: This is a statistical finding from correlation analysis.

claim: Module 1 and Module 5 are the most phylogenetically conserved modules.
source_text: Genes assigned in the LCA to Modules 1 (Figure 4B, blue entries) and 5 (Figure 4F, red entries) tend to persist in those modules (Module Stability 94% ± 0.5% and 84% ± 1.2%, respectively, 'Materials and methods').
evidence_reasoning: This is based on analysis of module stability across the phylogeny.

claim: Modules 2, 3, and 4 are less stable, with more frequent reassignment of their member genes to other modules.
source_text: Conversely, Modules 2, 3, and 4 (Figure 4C–E) are less stable, with more frequent reassignment of their member genes to other modules.
evidence_reasoning: This is based on analysis of module stability across the phylogeny.

claim: Module 1 and 5 are the least dynamic as reflected by the average proportion of genes that join or leave each module.
source_text: Module 1 and 5 are the least dynamic as reflected by the average proportion of genes that join (11% ± 1.6% and 17% ± 1.7%, respectively) or leave each module (6% ± 0.4% and 16% ± 1%, respectively) between each pair of ancestor and child species in the phylogeny
evidence_reasoning: This is based on calculation of Module Expansion and Contraction Indices.

claim: Cell cycle and DNA replication genes are reassigned in a coordinated fashion from Module 3 in the LCA to Modules 4 and 5 in S. cerevisiae and other post-WGD species.
source_text: For example, cell cycle and DNA replication genes are reassigned in a coordinated fashion from Module 3 in the LCA to Modules 4 and 5 in S. cerevisiae and other post-WGD species
evidence_reasoning: This is based on analysis of module assignments showing coordinated transitions.

claim: Mating and meiosis genes are reassigned from Module 1 in the LCA to Module 2 in S. cerevisiae and other post-WGD species.
source_text: mating and meiosis genes are reassigned from Module 1 in the LCA to Module 2 in S. cerevisiae and other post-WGD species
evidence_reasoning: This is based on analysis of module assignments showing coordinated transitions.

claim: Mitochondrial genes are reassigned from Module 1 in the LCA to Module 4 in post-WGD species and to Module 5 in S. pombe.
source_text: mitochondrial genes are reassigned from Module 1 in the LCA to Module 4 in post-WGD species and to Module 5 in S. pombe
evidence_reasoning: This is based on analysis of module assignments showing coordinated transitions.

claim: Oxidative phosphorylation genes are reassigned from Module 1 in the LCA to Module 5 in post-WGD species and S. pombe.
source_text: oxidative phosphorylation genes are reassigned from Module 1 in the LCA to Module 5 in post-WGD species and S. pombe
evidence_reasoning: This is based on analysis of module assignments showing coordinated transitions.

claim: Amino acid and purine metabolism genes are reassigned from Module 1 in the LCA to Module 5 in post-WGD species.
source_text: amino acid and purine metabolism genes are reassigned from Module 1 in the LCA to Module 5 in post-WGD species
evidence_reasoning: This is based on analysis of module assignments showing coordinated transitions.

claim: The reassignment of mitochondrial and respiratory genes is associated with changes in carbon lifestyle during the transitions to respiro-fermentation post-WGD and in S. pombe.
source_text: Particularly substantial transitions in module assignment are associated with changes in carbon lifestyle during the transitions to respiro-fermentation post-WGD and in S. pombe
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference from the coordinated reassignment patterns and known lifestyle differences.

claim: Mitochondrial and oxidative phosphorylation genes have significantly lower nucleosome occupancy at their 5′ NFRs in respiratory species compared to respiro-fermentative species.
source_text: Mitochondrial and oxidative phosphorylation genes have significantly lower nucleosome occupancy at their 5′ NFRs in respiratory species compared to respiro-fermentative species
evidence_reasoning: This is based on analysis of nucleosome positioning data from cited studies.

claim: Binding sites for several amino acid and purine metabolism TFs are depleted from NFRs in post-WGD species and enriched in pre-WGD species.
source_text: For each of 13 species (columns, tree), shown are the enrichment (yellow) or depletion (blue) in NFRs of binding sites for several amino acid and purine metabolism TFs (rows) whose sites are depleted from NFRs in post-WGD species and enriched in pre-WGD species.
evidence_reasoning: This is based on analysis of motif positioning relative to NFRs.

claim: The promoters of mRP and respiration genes have lost the binding site for the transcription factor Sfp1 in many respirofermentative species.
source_text: In addition, the promoters of mRP and respiration genes have lost the binding site for the transcription factor Sfp1 (previously identified as the 'Rapid Growth Element', RGE; Ihmels et al., 2005) in many respirofermentative species
evidence_reasoning: This is based on motif analysis and cited previous work.

claim: The Sfp1 binding site is strongly conserved in 'growth' (Module 1) genes across all species (except S. japonicus).
source_text: The Sfp1 binding site is strongly conserved in 'growth' (Module 1) genes across all species (except S. japonicus) and serves as an ancient regulatory tether of the growth module (p<0.05, Hyper-geometric test; Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence_reasoning: This is based on motif enrichment analysis across species.

claim: Purine metabolism and amino acid catabolism genes in pathways that feed nucleotide synthesis are reassigned from Module 1 in the LCA to Module 5 in post-WGD species.
source_text: Indeed, more surprisingly, purine metabolism and amino acid catabolism genes in pathways that feed nucleotide synthesis (Figure 8A) are reassigned from Module 1 in the LCA to Module 5 in post-WGD species
evidence_reasoning: This is based on analysis of module assignments for specific metabolic pathways.

claim: Many of the reassigned genes in carbon metabolism are WGD paralogs.
source_text: Many of the reassigned genes in carbon metabolism are WGD paralogs (Figure 8B)
evidence_reasoning: This is based on analysis of paralog status of reassigned genes.

claim: Genes that were never duplicated have a lower tendency to be reassigned than genes with a duplication event.
source_text: Genes that have a paralog were more likely to change their module assignment than those present in a single copy (KS test, p<1.5 × 10−107).
evidence_reasoning: This is a statistical finding from comparing duplicated and non-duplicated genes.

claim: Paralogous genes are much more likely to be reassigned after duplication than their corresponding pre-duplication orthologs.
source_text: Furthermore, controlling for any differences in function between duplicated and non-duplicated genes, paralogous genes are much more likely to be reassigned after duplication than their corresponding pre-duplication orthologs (Figure 10D,E, KS test, p<1 × 10−18).
evidence_reasoning: This is a statistical finding from comparing pre- and post-duplication reassignment rates.

claim: The increased divergence was most prominent at the WGD ancestor (A5) and the Schizosaccharomyces ancestor (A13).
source_text: This increased divergence was most prominent at the WGD ancestor (A5) and the Schizosaccharomyces ancestor (A13) (Figure 10A).
evidence_reasoning: This is based on analysis of AMCI values at different phylogenetic points.

claim: Both ancestors (A5 and A13) have a larger number of retained paralog pairs compared to other ancestral species.
source_text: Both ancestors also have a larger number of retained paralog pairs compared to other ancestral species
evidence_reasoning: This is based on counting paralog pairs at different phylogenetic points.

claim: The reassigned paralogs are enriched in carbon metabolism genes.
source_text: Consistently, the reassigned paralogs are enriched in carbon metabolism genes (Figure 10—source data 1).
evidence_reasoning: This is based on GO enrichment analysis of reassigned paralogs.

claim: Approximately 60% of the paralog pairs that arose at the ancestor of the Candida clade (A10) and that will eventually change their assignment, do so at that ancestor.
source_text: For example, ∼60% of the paralog pairs that arose at the ancestor of the Candida clade (A10) and that will eventually change their assignment, do so at that ancestor.
evidence_reasoning: This is based on analysis of the timing of paralog reassignment.

claim: Of all the paralog pairs that arose sporadically (not in the WGD) in the phylogeny, and where at least one member of the pair was subsequently reassigned to a different module, 53% do so 'at' the point at which they arose.
source_text: Overall, of all the paralog pairs that arose sporadically (not in the WGD) in the phylogeny, and where at least one member of the pair was subsequently reassigned to a different module, 53% do so 'at' the point at which they arose.
evidence_reasoning: This is based on analysis of the timing of paralog reassignment.

claim: Sporadically duplicated genes are significantly enriched among all the reassigned genes at their point of duplication, but not at later phylogenetic points.
source_text: Furthermore, such sporadically duplicated genes are significantly enriched (Hyper-geometric test, p<0.05,) among all the reassigned genes (duplicated or not) at their point of duplication, but not at later phylogenetic points, when they behave comparably to non-duplicated genes (Figure 10B).
evidence_reasoning: This is based on enrichment analysis at different phylogenetic points.

claim: There is a short 'window of opportunity' in regulatory innovation, specifically facilitated by paralogous genes shortly after they are duplicated but not later.
source_text: This suggests a short 'window of opportunity' in regulatory innovation, specifically facilitated by paralogous genes shortly after they are duplicated but not later
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference from the temporal pattern of paralog reassignment.

claim: Paralogs that arose in the WGD are enriched among reassigned genes not only at the WGD ancestor but also at later phylogenetic points.
source_text: Paralogs that arose in the WGD (Figure 10B, white circles) are enriched among reassigned genes not only at the WGD ancestor but also at later phylogenetic points
evidence_reasoning: This is based on enrichment analysis at different phylogenetic points.

claim: Segmental duplication rarely preserves the entire regulatory region resulting in immediate expression divergence.
source_text: This may be explained by the fact that segmental duplication rarely preserves the entire regulatory region resulting in immediate expression divergence (Lynch and Katju, 2004)
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference based on cited knowledge about duplication mechanisms.

claim: Duplicates from WGD events preserve the regulatory inputs and thus may take longer to diverge.
source_text: whereas duplicates from WGD events preserve the regulatory inputs and thus may take longer to diverge.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference about the mechanism underlying the observed pattern.

claim: Mitochondrial and respiratory genes were reassigned en masse in both independent evolutions of respiro-fermentation, accompanied by convergent cis regulatory changes.
source_text: In both cases, mitochondrial and respiratory genes were reassigned en masse, accompanied by convergent cis regulatory changes.
evidence_reasoning: This is based on analysis of module reassignments and motif changes in both lineages.

claim: Changes in the regulation of amino acid, purine and sulfur metabolism genes occurred only following the WGD.
source_text: However, changes in the regulation of amino acid, purine and sulfur metabolism genes occurred only following the WGD, possibly by repositioning of cis-regulatory elements relative to nucleosome free regions.
evidence_reasoning: This is based on analysis of module reassignments and motif positioning specific to post-WGD species.

claim: Many of the changes occurred gradually, with only some noticeable in K. polysporus, the first species to have diverged post-WGD.
source_text: The post-WGD event can be monitored in fine phylogenetic resolution, showing that many of the changes occurred gradually, with only some noticeable in K. polysporus, the first species to have diverged post-WGD.
evidence_reasoning: This is based on analysis of expression patterns in K. polysporus relative to other species.

claim: Respiro-fermentation is functionally analogous to the Warburg Effect in cancer cells.
source_text: Respiro-fermentation is functionally analogous to the (somatically evolved) Warburg Effect in cancer cells (Vander Heiden et al., 2009)
evidence_reasoning: This is a conceptual analogy supported by citation.

claim: There are well-known similarities in glycolysis and respiration between respiro-fermentation in yeast and the Warburg Effect in cancer that enable both to direct glucose to biosynthesis.
source_text: There are well-known similarities in glycolysis and respiration between the two states that enable both cancer and yeast cells to direct glucose to biosynthesis, supporting their rapid growth and proliferation.
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about metabolic similarities.

claim: The observation that genes encoding enzymes in the nucleotide salvage and glycine biosynthesis pathways are strongly induced post-diauxic shift in respiro-fermentative post-WGD species is analogous to recently identified changes in these pathways in cancer cells that display the Warburg Effect.
source_text: The observation that genes encoding enzymes in the nucleotide salvage and glycine biosynthesis pathways are strongly induced post-diauxic shift in respiro-fermentative post-WGD species is analogous to recently identified changes in these pathways in cancer cells that display the Warburg Effect (Gaglio et al., 2011; Jain et al., 2012)
evidence_reasoning: This is based on the experimental data and comparison to cited cancer studies.

claim: Rewiring of nucleotide biosynthetic pathways contributes to the respiro-fermentative phenotype.
source_text: suggests that rewiring of nucleotide biosynthetic pathways contributes to this phenotype
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference from the observed changes in nucleotide metabolism genes.

claim: Most paralogs (66% of all pairs) have at least one member diverging from the ancestral module.
source_text: Most paralogs (66% of all pairs) have at least one member diverging from the ancestral module.
evidence_reasoning: This is based on analysis of paralog module assignments relative to pre-duplication ancestors.

claim: 27% of all paralog pairs show 'classical' neo-functionalization, where one paralog maintains the ancestral assignment and the other is assigned to a different module.
source_text: This includes paralogs with distinct fates, either due to 'classical' neo-functionalization (27% of all pairs), where one paralog maintains the ancestral assignment and the other is assigned to a different module
evidence_reasoning: This is based on classification of paralog fates from module assignments.

claim: 12% of paralog pairs show asymmetric divergence, where each paralog is reassigned to a distinct module, each different than the ancestral one.
source_text: or due to asymmetric divergence (12%), where each paralog is reassigned to a distinct module, each different than the ancestral one
evidence_reasoning: This is based on classification of paralog fates from module assignments.

claim: 27% of paralog pairs show symmetric divergence, where both paralogs are reassigned to the same module, distinct from the ancestral one.
source_text: In the remaining cases (27%) there is symmetric divergence, where both paralogs are reassigned to the same module, distinct from the ancestral one
evidence_reasoning: This is based on classification of paralog fates from module assignments.

claim: Only in a minority of paralog pairs (34%) the ancestral assignment of both copies is conserved.
source_text: Only in a minority of paralog pairs (34%) the ancestral assignment of both copies is conserved
evidence_reasoning: This is based on classification of paralog fates from module assignments.

claim: The pre-duplication orthologs of genes from the neo-functionalized class are most prominent in the 'unchanged' Module 3 and mildly induced Module 4.
source_text: The pre-duplication orthologs of genes from the neo-functionalized class are most prominent in the 'unchanged' Module 3 and mildly induced Module 4 (Hyper-geometric test, p<10−3)
evidence_reasoning: This is based on enrichment analysis of pre-duplication module assignments.

claim: Genes that were not regulated in glucose depletion prior to duplication 'gain' such regulation de novo post-duplication, for at least one paralog.
source_text: suggesting that genes that were not regulated in glucose depletion prior to duplication, 'gain' such regulation de novo post-duplication, for at least one paralog.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference from the enrichment of neo-functionalized genes in unchanged modules.

claim: Neo-functionalization has contributed to the regulatory divergence of key genes in carbon metabolism during the evolution of respiro-fermentation.
source_text: Neo-functionalization has also contributed to the regulatory divergence of key genes in carbon metabolism during the evolution of respiro-fermentation (Figure 8B), consistent with previous studies (Conant and Wolfe, 2007).
evidence_reasoning: This is based on analysis of carbon metabolism genes and consistent with cited work.

claim: Similarity in heat stress profiles is inversely proportional to phylogenetic distance.
source_text: As in the response to glucose depletion, similarity in heat stress profiles is inversely proportional to phylogenetic distance (Figure 11C–F)
evidence_reasoning: This is based on correlation analysis of heat shock expression profiles.

claim: The strongly repressed Module 1, which consists of 'growth' genes, is the most conserved in heat shock response.
source_text: and the strongly repressed Module 1, which consists of 'growth' genes, is the most conserved (Roy et al., 2013).
evidence_reasoning: This is based on analysis of heat shock data as cited.

claim: The evolutionary trajectories of paralogous genes in heat shock are highly similar to those in glucose depletion.
source_text: Furthermore, the evolutionary trajectories of paralogous genes—including the higher reassignment of paralogs, the distinct reassignment capacity of sporadic and large-scale duplications, and the preponderance of reassignment of only one of two paralogs—are highly similar between heat shock and glucose depletion (Figure 11A,B).
evidence_reasoning: This is based on comparative analysis of paralog behavior in both conditions.

claim: The patterns observed are general evolutionary principles, at least in this phylogeny.
source_text: This suggests that these are general evolutionary principles, at least in this phylogeny.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference from the similarity of patterns across two different conditions.

claim: Considering both conditions allows refinement of the classification of paralog fates.
source_text: The additional condition allows us to further refine the classification of paralog fates
evidence_reasoning: This is a methodological inference about the value of multiple conditions.

claim: Some paralogs are conserved in both responses.
source_text: some paralogs are conserved in both responses (Figure 12A)
evidence_reasoning: This is based on analysis of module assignments in both conditions.

claim: Some paralogs are neo-functionalized in one paralog in both responses.
source_text: some are neo-functionalized in one paralog in both responses (Figure 12B)
evidence_reasoning: This is based on analysis of module assignments in both conditions.

claim: Some paralogs are neo-functionalized in both paralogs but in different ways in each response.
source_text: some are neo-functionalized in both paralogs but in different ways in each response (Figure 12C)
evidence_reasoning: This is based on analysis of module assignments in both conditions.

claim: Some paralogs show sub-functionalization, where each paralog maintains the ancestral assignment in one response but not the other.
source_text: and some show sub-functionalization, where each paralog maintains the ancestral assignment in one response but not the other (Figure 12D)
evidence_reasoning: This is based on analysis of module assignments in both conditions.

claim: The substantial overall conservation observed in the response exceeds that reported in other studies.
source_text: The substantial overall conservation we observed in the response—exceeding that reported in other studies (Tirosh et al. 2011), indicates the robustness of our experimental strategy.
evidence_reasoning: This is a comparison of the current results to cited previous work.

claim: The expression profiles in each species for a set of genes identified as regulated by growth rate in S. cerevisiae are similar across species in the phylogeny.
source_text: First, the expression profiles in each species for a set of genes recently identified as regulated by growth rate in S. cerevisiae (Brauer et al., 2008) are similar across species in the phylogeny (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A), consistent with our physiological sampling.
evidence_reasoning: This is based on analysis of growth-regulated genes and comparison to cited work.

claim: Removal of growth-regulated genes did not significantly change the correlation of global expression profiles at any of the points other than lag phase.
source_text: Indeed, removal of these genes did not significantly change the correlation of global expression profiles (p>0.1, paired t-test) at any of the points other than lag phase
evidence_reasoning: This is based on statistical analysis after removing growth genes.

evidence_reasoning: This is based on correlation analysis between distant species.

claim: Arboretum incorporates the species and gene phylogenetic relationships to identify modules in each species and to reconstruct the evolutionary trajectory of each gene's module assignment from the LCA.
source_text: To systematically compare the responses of the different species to glucose depletion we developed Arboretum, a probabilistic algorithm, which incorporates the species and gene phylogenetic relationships to identify modules in each species and to reconstruct the evolutionary trajectory of each gene's module assignment from the LCA
evidence_reasoning: This describes the computational method developed.

claim: Arboretum uses a generative probabilistic model that explicitly models the evolution of module membership along the phylogeny.
source_text: Arboretum uses a generative probabilistic model that explicitly models the evolution of module membership along the phylogeny, and uses the gene tree structure to handle complex orthology and paralogy relationships.
evidence_reasoning: This describes features of the computational method.

claim: A relatively small number of modules (k = 5) was chosen as a conservative choice, which may under-estimate divergence relative to conservation.
source_text: We chose a relatively small number (k = 5) as a conservative choice, which may under-estimate divergence relative to conservation, since genes with minor differences in expression between species would still likely belong to the same module.
evidence_reasoning: This is a methodological choice with reasoning about its implications.

claim: This choice increases confidence in those divergence events that are highlighted, but may miss other divergence events.
source_text: This choice increases our confidence in those divergence events that are highlighted, but may miss other divergence events.

claim: The correspondence between the overall trends based on the direct expression levels and those based on Arboretum modules supports the validity of the choice of k = 5.
source_text: Several lines of evidence support the validity of our choice including the correspondence between the overall trends based on the direct expression levels (e.g., Figure 3) and those based on Arboretum modules
evidence_reasoning: This is validation of the methodological choice through comparison of results.

claim: The module assignments at the point of duplication are two independent draws of module membership, one each for copy.
source_text: In particular, the module assignments at the point of duplication are two independent draws of module membership, one each for copy, ensuring that the orthogroup has the same module assignment before the duplication and allowing it the freedom to change assignment after duplication.
evidence_reasoning: This describes how the algorithm handles duplication events.

source_text: Furthermore, the microarray profiles are highly correlated to corresponding profiles measured using RNA-Seq data generated from RNA extracted from the same plateau and mid-log time point samples. This is true both when considering all genes (0.835 < r < 0.958, mean r = 0.913, 0.0362 SD) and when considering only paralogs (0.849 < r < 0.965, mean r = 0.924, 0.0368 SD)

claim: Several studies showed increased transcriptional divergence of paralogous genes in S. cerevisiae compared to non-duplicated genes.
source_text: In particular, several studies (Teichmann and Babu, 2004; Gu et al., 2004, 2005; Conant and Wolfe, 2006) showed increased transcriptional divergence of paralogous genes in S. cerevisiae compared to non-duplicated genes, consistent with a model of accelerated transcriptional evolution following duplication (Gu et al., 2005).

source_text: However, since such studies typically compared the expression of paralogous genes in only one or two species (Teichmann and Babu, 2004; Gu et al., 2004, 2005; Conant and Wolfe, 2006; Guan et al., 2007; Tirosh and Barkai, 2007), they could not reliably infer the ancestral state
evidence_reasoning: This is a critique of previous studies based on their methodological limitations.

claim: The framework for comparative functional genomics is applicable to any complex phylogeny.
source_text: Our framework for comparative functional genomics is applicable to any complex phylogeny, and can help test these principles of regulatory evolution in other responses and species.

claim: Studies relying on cis-regulatory sequences are more prevalent than functional studies of comparative gene regulation.
source_text: While studies relying on cis-regulatory sequences are more prevalent, functional studies of comparative gene regulation are beginning to shed light on how regulatory evolution is linked to functional changes.

claim: Comparative genomics approaches have allowed us to begin to trace the evolution of gene regulation at different time scales.

claim: Studies in yeast showed that while co-expression of genes in modules can be conserved at substantial distances, the associated regulatory mechanisms often diverge.

evidence_reasoning: This summarizes findings from cited previous studies in yeast.

claim: Evolutionary changes in regulators contribute toward different paths through a 'hybrid' regulatory state for the ancestral regulatory network to be resolved to generate the diversity of regulatory network structures observed in modern species.
source_text: Importantly, evolutionary changes in regulators, facilitated by protein modularity, in cooperative binding with other factors and shifts in protein–DNA interactions contribute toward different paths through a 'hybrid' regulatory state for the ancestral regulatory network to be resolved in to generate the diversity of regulatory network structures observed in modern species (Baker et al., 2011, 2012; Tuch et al., 2008a)
evidence_reasoning: This is a model of regulatory evolution supported by citations.

claim: Most experimental studies rely on two to four species, with few exceptions.
source_text: Despite these early successes, collecting experimental data across species has remained challenging, and hence most experimental studies rely on two to four species (Tanay et al., 2005; Tirosh et al., 2006; Lelandais et al., 2008; Wittkopp et al., 2008), with few exceptions (Schmidt et al., 2010; Tsankov et al., 2010; Wapinski et al., 2010; Brawand et al., 2011; He et al., 2011).

claim: An important challenge is to collect experimental data in such a way that would minimize irrelevant differences due to growth conditions.

claim: Expanding the experimental scope to cover a broader phylogenetic range and density can help study the divergence of expression in individual genes and gene modules.
source_text: Expanding the experimental scope to cover a broader phylogenetic range and density can help study the divergence of expression in individual genes and gene modules in order to answer questions on the extent of conservation of transcriptional programs, its relation to phylogenetic distance, the emergence of new regulatory patterns across modules of co-regulated genes, and the specific contribution of gene duplication and divergence
